journey.title: Open the filters drawer and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: When the drawer is opened via the button, focus remains on the triggering button or the body instead of moving inside the dialog, preventing keyboard users from interacting with the filter controls.
plan.repair_strategy: Override the _onBeforeShow method in the Drawer class to move focus to the close button (#filters-close) after initializing swipe gestures, ensuring the dialog receives initial focus upon opening.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Upon opening the filters drawer, focus will be placed on the close button, allowing users to press Tab to navigate to the 'In stock' checkbox and interact with the form using only the keyboard.
functional_risks: If the close button is absent or dynamically removed, the focus attempt will be safely skipped due to the null check.
The focus change occurs after swipe initialization, preserving existing touch/swipe behavior.
verification_requirements: After activating the filters button with Enter, the active element must be #filters-close.
Subsequent Tab presses must move focus to #in-stock, then #waterproof, then #apply, and loop correctly.
Pressing Space on a checkbox must toggle its checked state.
Pressing Enter on the 'Show results' button must update the applied filter output and close the drawer.

attempts.failure: Patch hardcodes the test page into component code: js/src/drawer.ts now names #filters-close. Component code must work on any page that uses it; repair the component's behaviour without referring to this page's ids.

plan.root_cause: The _onBeforeShow() method in drawer.ts hardcodes the test page's specific ID '#filters-close' when focusing the close button. Component code must work generically on any page using the drawer, not reference page-specific IDs.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the hardcoded ID selector with a generic selector that finds the drawer's dismiss button using the standard Bootstrap data attribute pattern [data-bs-dismiss="drawer"]. This works on any page because the dismiss button is marked with this attribute in the component's markup contract.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Upon opening any drawer, focus will be placed on the drawer's close button (identified by data-bs-dismiss="drawer"), allowing keyboard users to immediately press Tab to navigate into the drawer's content and interact with form controls.
functional_risks: If a drawer lacks a dismiss button with data-bs-dismiss="drawer", the focus attempt is safely skipped due to the null check.
The focus change occurs after swipe initialization, preserving existing touch/swipe behavior.
verification_requirements: After activating the filters button with Enter, the active element must be the drawer's close button (data-bs-dismiss="drawer").
Subsequent Tab presses must move focus to the first focusable element in the drawer (e.g., #in-stock checkbox), then through other controls.
Pressing Space on a checkbox must toggle its checked state.
Pressing Enter on the 'Show results' button must update the applied filter output and close the drawer.
Pressing Escape must close the drawer and return focus to the trigger button.

attempts.failure: Edit 1 (js/src/drawer.ts): before does not occur in the file. 3 of its lines are not in the source. not in file: "const closeBtn = this._element.querySelector('#filters-close')"; closest is line 133: "const navbar = this._element.closest('.navbar')" | not in file: "if (closeBtn) {" | not in file: "closeBtn.focus({ preventScroll: true })"; closest is line 204: "this.focus({ preventScroll: true })". Best alignment: before lines 1-2 match file lines 110-111, then before line 3 "const closeBtn = this._element.querySelector('#filters-close')" differs from file line 112 "}". The real file lines are in actual_source_region. Copy before verbatim from source_candidates.

plan.root_cause: The _onBeforeShow() method in drawer.ts only initializes swipe gestures but does not move focus into the drawer when it opens. Keyboard users cannot interact with the drawer's content because focus remains on the trigger button or body.
plan.repair_strategy: Override _onBeforeShow() to focus the drawer's dismiss button (identified by the standard data-bs-dismiss="drawer" attribute) after initializing swipe. This works generically across all pages using the drawer component.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Upon opening any drawer, focus moves to the dismiss button, allowing keyboard users to immediately press Tab to navigate into the drawer's content and interact with form controls.
functional_risks: If a drawer lacks a dismiss button with data-bs-dismiss="drawer", the focus attempt is safely skipped due to the null check.
The focus change occurs after swipe initialization, preserving existing touch/swipe behavior.
verification_requirements: After activating the filters button with Enter, the active element must be the drawer's close button (data-bs-dismiss="drawer").
Subsequent Tab presses must move focus to the first focusable element in the drawer (e.g., #in-stock checkbox), then through other controls.
Pressing Space on a checkbox must toggle its checked state.
Pressing Enter on the 'Show results' button must update the applied filter output and close the drawer.
Pressing Escape must close the drawer and return focus to the trigger button.
